passage:
On Friday afternoon, SpaceX's Starship took off from the company's base in Texas, near the border between the U.S. and Mexico. Starship is the largest and most powerful rocket in the world. It is 124 meters tall. This was its 15th flight since 2023, but only its second trip to orbit.

The rocket has two parts. The bottom part is called the booster, and the top part is the spacecraft. After the two parts separated, the spacecraft flew into orbit and released 26 Starlink satellites. It stayed about 265 kilometers above the Earth and went around the planet 14 times. On the mission before this one, it went around only once or twice.

The booster did not have a good day. On its way back down, its engines stopped too early. Its guidance system knew it was in the wrong place, so it turned away over the water and destroyed itself. Pieces of it were left in the Gulf of Mexico. Engineers are still trying to find out why this happened.

The spacecraft did much better. On Saturday, 22 hours after it left, it came back to the same launch pad. Giant mechanical arms on the launch tower caught it in midair. It was the first time a Starship returning from space was caught this way. SpaceX said its heat shield and everything else seemed to work well. Elon Musk called it an "epic day." He even hugged the spacecraft.

Catching a rocket means it can be used again, and this makes space travel faster and cheaper. SpaceX had hoped to catch both parts this time, but it caught only one. Still, it had already caught boosters three times before.

NASA is paying billions of dollars for Starship to help carry astronauts to the moon. NASA's leader, Jared Isaacman, said, "It was almost magic." NASA hopes to land people on the moon as soon as 2028. That would be the first moon landing in more than 50 years. Musk has an even bigger dream: he wants to build a city on Mars.
stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: A new rocket base that SpaceX is building in Mexico
Starship's spacecraft was caught after a trip to orbit, but its booster was lost
Why NASA decided to stop working with SpaceX
How astronauts live on the moon
explain: 正解是選項二。全文在講 Starship 飛上軌道，太空船回來時被發射塔的機械手臂接住（the first time a Starship returning from space was caught），但推進器在回程時自毀（destroyed itself）。選項一：發射基地在 Texas，文章沒說要在墨西哥蓋基地。選項三：NASA 還在付錢給 Starship，沒有停止合作。選項四：文章沒有談太空人怎麼在月球生活。

options: Once or twice
15 times
14 times
26 times
explain: 正解是選項三。文中寫 went around the planet 14 times。選項一：once or twice 是上一次任務的圈數。選項二：15 是 Starship 自 2023 年以來的第 15 次飛行，不是圈數。選項四：26 是放出的 Starlink 衛星數量。
